mercurial

/mer-KYOOR-ee-ul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Mercurial means marked by rapid, unpredictable changes in mood or behavior.

The band's mercurial drummer could go from laughing at breakfast to storming out of rehearsal by noon.

Example

No one on the kitchen staff could predict which version of Chef Alvarez would walk in each morning. On Monday he praised a line cook's sauce so warmly that she blushed; on Tuesday he sent the very same sauce back three times without explaining why. By Friday he was cheerfully handing out pastries he had baked at dawn for the whole crew. The staff learned to read his mercurial moods the way sailors read a changing sky.

The chef's moods shifted quickly and without warning from day to day, which is exactly what mercurial describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unpredictable: Unpredictable means impossible to anticipate from one moment to the next, and it applies to anything - weather, traffic, a bouncing ball. Mercurial is unpredictability located in a person's moods: the swings are rapid and nobody can guess the next one. A schedule can be unpredictable; only a temperament can be mercurial.

temperamental: Temperamental means prone to sudden shifts of mood, and it carries a note of complaint about machines and divas alike - a temperamental printer, a temperamental soprano. Mercurial keeps the speed but adds range and a certain shimmer: the person swings between entirely different selves, delightful one hour and thunderous the next. Temperamental grumbles; mercurial dazzles and alarms by turns.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

steady: consistent and dependable in mood

even-tempered: calm and not easily upset

Where it sits · how unstable the temperament is

moody → mercurial → volatile

moody vs. mercurial: A moody person slips in and out of low spirits, while a mercurial one swings between entirely different moods with startling speed.

volatile vs. mercurial: A mercurial temperament changes quickly, but a volatile one goes a step further, ready to erupt at the slightest spark.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — Mercuri: from Mercury, the swift Roman messenger god, whose name also belongs to the fastest-moving planet

Suffix — -al: characteristic of, pertaining to, having the nature of

Put it together: Mercurial attaches the suffix -al, meaning 'characteristic of,' to the name of Mercury, the Roman messenger god famed for darting anywhere in an instant, whose name also belongs to the planet that races fastest around the sun. To be mercurial is literally to be 'characteristic of Mercury,' changing direction as swiftly as the god himself.

Use the root in a new word: mercury: The Romans' messenger god Mercury lends his name twice: to the fastest-moving planet and to the liquid metal mercury. Alchemists liked matching metals to the heavens — gold for the sun, silver for the moon — and this restless, silvery metal struck them as belonging to the messenger god: it never stays put.

Word Building

Word Choice

literary, character-description register

Mercurial is about pure unpredictability, not unfriendliness. A mercurial person may be delightful one hour and thunderous the next; the point is that no one can tell which is coming. It most often modifies temper, moods, temperament, or the person directly.
